lines: The taxi's headlights are out, no glow,
yet it still claims it's part of the show.
I watch it speed past with no working brake,
if this is service, I'll never take.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She pauses at the garden's edge, her breath a thread,
the silence ahead feels too vast to be dread.
A glint in the grass draws her close, so near,
and the world holds still—this moment is dear.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: She hums the verse but she sings it all wrong,
then gets stuck where the chorus should belong.
She tries to skip ahead with a sudden leap,
but ends up humming the bridge instead—she's quite deep.
He holds a cup with both hands, bright and clean,
his voice lifts up with a song unseen.
A smile spreads wide across his weathered face,
he catches joy, even in this place.
You dig your tiny claws into the ground,
each acorn buried like a secret found.
You run back fast, though you're not quite sure
if this time, the earth will keep it pure.
I stare at the empty square, lost in a clue,
the answer's there, but I can't grasp the true.
I keep my pen still, watching the clock take its seat,
this quiet moment feels like a small treat.
It starts again at noon with a loud beep,
she groans like the machine's asking her to keep.
"I'm not awake," she says, "and I still need more too,"
her eyes are half shut and her mood is pure blue.
My eyes snap open to a world of dread,
my mind still trapped in dreams of stale bread.
The clock insists I've slept too long,
but nothing feels quite right, not even the wrong.
I watch the feather drift through the sky,
I can't stop asking why it won't fly.
It clings to the branch, too thin to be still,
and I wait too long before I climb the hill.
You swipe a fry with a quick, guilty steal,
they don't notice, still mid-meal, still real.
You grab one more from the edge of their side,
you eat it slow, eyes full of quiet pride.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You unfold it and your face lights up with a smile,
just holding it close for a quiet awhile.
There's a note written small but it lifts the whole sky,
and you feel like laughing, right up to the high.
She's stuck in traffic, lost in a zone,
mumbling complaints to her dog, all alone.
Her playlist's looping a song she can't track,
she turns down the music and plays it back.
You stare too long at the screen's soft glow,
it's giving you dreams that don't quite show.
Your eyes feel warm, but you just can't turn,
the light down—your night has a new burn.
She didn't need a laser—her ruler could slide
with calm precision and quiet pride.
It traced each edge, every boundary, each line,
until no detail escaped her sharp fine.
The machine says I've got something wrong,
but I just wanted to pay for my song.
It keeps asking for a new bill,
and I stand here, waiting, still.
I let the record spin with a little grin,
the needle settles deep, takes the tune in.
A soft crackle hums through the quiet air,
then the music pulls me right back there.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: I stir my cocoa with a plastic spoon,
it's glowing warm, not cool, not too soon.
The milk turns into lazy little steam,
I almost fall asleep, mid-sip, mid-dream.
You piled those files so high they look like a stack,
one slip and the whole thing will crack.
The top folder wobbles, then takes a wild fall,
it lands flat against the kitchen wall.
The bus driver slumps in his seat,
his head tilts down—no sign of retreat.
The bus rolls on, no one calls the stop,
he's still there when we finally top.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: The screen's dim glow shows a number too low,
they stare at the count like it holds the world's glow.
They wait for a new notification next,
the silence hums louder than any text.
You forgot it in the corner—now it's gone mold,
the last bite tastes like something long left cold.
Your back feels heavy from the weight of the bag,
and every step reminds you why it's all sag.
They argue over who paid what cost,
still counting the bill to see who lost.
One finally pulls out their phone to show
the math is wrong, and it's all too slow.
My feet are screaming, blistered and sore,
I stand before the closet's closed door.
I tie the laces tight, they hold me in place,
I walk through life with a quiet grace.
You leave your dog curled on the soft fur,
he stirs a little as he starts to purr.
I tug the blanket where the drool has spread,
but keep the thread of warmth beneath my head.
You wake with your neck locked in a stubborn ache,
like something's driven deep into your stake.
You sit on the floor and you blink at the door,
and wonder why your body still wants more.
You pull out the jammed paper, soft as a sheet,
the edges worn where you once used to meet
the same old print job comes out in a roll,
dust still lives in your printer's tired soul.
I burned toast in the hotel kitchen mess,
it's not like I've never done this before, less.
The smoke alarm chirps with a dirty ash,
I throw the plate down and leave it with a dash.
The stack leans too far, I'm afraid it'll fall,
my hands tremble as I try to hold it all.
I didn't know it'd be this much of a mess,
I should've just said no, but I said yes.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: Her face was tight with a sudden frown,
she looked away, still holding her down.
But in that blur, something was caught—
a quiet smile beneath the thought.
It rolls across the floor with no care at all,
then stops right between the door and the wall.
She tries to step but her foot's stuck in the way,
so she laughs and stays there to play.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: They sit too still by the fire's warm hill,
their hands clutch too tight, like something will spill.
The logs crack and spit as the air grows close,
and then the room lights up with a sudden rose.
I reach for one fry without a sound to steal,
the warmth still there, and the guilt starts to feel.
It tastes like childhood, sharp and faintly salt,
I know I should've asked—now I'm caught in the fault.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the sky turn soft and deep blue,
as shadows creep across the lawn through.
Don't rush ahead—just stand here and stay,
let the storm come close but keep it away.
I stand in the aisle with my hands full of care,
watching every word float up through the air.
I read each line till I know what's fine,
the truth behind the label's quiet sign.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The heat climbs fast and my skin starts to rise,
I blink but the sweat won't stop from my eyes.
It rolls down slow where the temple meets the drip,
I wipe it quick before I take another trip.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You blow so hard you make the flame go fast,
the wick still dances but it doesn't last.
One breath, and silence wraps the room like a snap,
you've erased the glow from every candle's map.
The screen freezes mid-sentence, play turns to gray,
I don't know if I'll watch this show today.
The moment slipped away, the plot's now all gone,
I sit here, still waiting for it to go on.
You take the path where the trees let go their gold,
the wind hums something that's been quietly told.
There's still time to step into the slowest chance,
and twist your coat around the autumn's dance.
You carry it through the hall and the back,
no moment feels light, though you don't quite lack.
The old straps press down, a comfort, not a weight,
you open the door and step out through the gate.
You pause, just looking at the salt on the grain,
a moment caught like a memory again.
It's the same old kitchen, the worn wooden floor,
and somehow this little spill brings more.
Your fingers fit in my palm like a key,
we stand there quiet, no need to be free.
You turn slowly and I follow along,
our steps match perfect, though neither's quite wrong.
The radio cuts out mid-song, you lose the tune,
but the stars still rise through the soft summer moon.
You push the button—just once—and hear a sound now,
a new song begins, and you feel your spirit bow.
You press the gas but the speed feels too fast,
your hands stay tight, like you're gripping the last.
The road ahead turns sharp, the wind climbs too high,
and now you fear what's up there in the sky.
They open the cupboard with a silent peek,
and take one cookie without a word or squeak.
They leave the jar half-full, but still ask for more,
the chocolate bar's gone—someone ate it all before.
You left the receipts in a cluttered mess,
now you can't find the one you need for less.
You dig through the stack just to make a claim,
the phone buzzes—your bank's sending a flame.
Each snowflake melts as it hits the fall,
I watch them vanish on the woolen wall.
The sky still promises a quiet show,
but here, my coat feels the weight of the flow.
The app says my fare is finally clear,
I breathe deep, like this moment's sincere.
I've waited all week—this is my prime,
I'm not stuck here, not wasting my time.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: A single flame cuts through the dark without name,
I don't know how long it will stay the same.
But in this quiet, my hands still keep the glow,
the light will show me where to go.
She leaves her socks inside the basket, deep
they stay there long after she's gone to sleep.
A shirt still holds the ghost of last week's stain,
like tears she never let herself feel in the rain.
You remember where it fell, right in the spot,
the last time you laughed, now you're stuck without a hot.
You shake the cushion, feel something near the edge,
and yes—the phone is there, still breathing on the ledge.
My back's been screaming since I sat down to ache,
so I stand and stretch, though it only makes me shake.
I touch my toes, but my hips still pull at the floor,
and now I'm mad I didn't take more time before.
You hear the rain on the roof like a drum,
you tap your thumb to match the slow hum.
The time ticks past but the rhythm stays on the clock,
you sit still as if the world's stopped in a block.
I catch a hint of summer rain,
it lingers soft, like a memory again.
I breathe deep in the passenger seat,
a quiet joy, a small treat.
Their old cat licks the kitchen wall with a grin,
a slow tongue, a habit from long ago, thin.
The sun dips low, the light starts to fall,
she's still there, licking the same wall.
She laughs so hard it's clearly fake,
she's not even close to the cake.
She falls to the floor in a full-body fit,
then says she forgot the funny bit.
You claim you slept through the whole night and the lie
still hangs heavy above your tired sky.
You slump in your chair like you're glued to the floor,
with coffee and regret and nothing to restore.
You've piled them high in a neat little stack,
each receipt aligned like a soldier on attack.
You left your keys in the coat pocket at home,
but you found every receipt—no need to roam.
You check your pocket—earbuds are gone,
you tap your phone but nothing's on.
The battery's dead, the case is flat,
you wonder where they got stuck at.
He left a mess where he lay down to rest,
but the dog's drool was pure joy—yes, that's blessed.
She laughs and wipes the couch, doesn't even frown,
old fur coat earned its place on that soft crown.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: You scroll past old photos, some still in blue,
the same blue sky, just fading through.
You open the screen like you're standing at the door,
time's dust settles where your feet once walked the floor.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She's caught mid-step, hair all in a blur,
the dog's tail flung wild, a streak of fur.
That quiet grin—her brother's wide, warm grin—
we were still young, and close, and just kin.
You push through crowds like you're on a crush,
but no one listens when you whisper "hush."
The doors close tight and you're stuck in the stand,
just another grain lost in the sand.
You wake to fire through the frost-lit red,
the world still wrapped in silence and dread.
A single sound splits the ice from its back,
the sky bleeds gold and the dark retreats to black.
I baked the cake with care and set it down,
he knocked it off with a wag and a frown.
Now crumbs are scattered, I can't place the blame,
but I still call him my sweet little name.
You let the tears fall when the music goes low,
but still you hum along, though your voice won't quite go.
You know the ache is real, though it doesn't feel true,
and still you keep breathing—because you're here, you.
You stand there in your coat, the world's a hiss,
remembering the last time you missed him this.
That old sidewalk smile still plays on your grin,
like the warmth from a memory gone thin.
A single drop hangs from the spoon's tip,
she holds it tight with her steady grip.
It swings and sways in a slow, shiny trail,
the jar is still full—no need to fail.
You step outside and the world's all aglow with shine,
the frost makes every blade look sharp and fine.
It's crisp and bright, and the sky's so clear,
you can almost touch the morning, warm and near.
The music cuts just as the chorus fades low,
she stops humming, still staring at the show.
Her thumb hovers near the screen, but there's no play,
she lets the silence settle—no way back today.
My banana's ripened just enough to peel,
the perfect mush for my morning meal.
The skin's gone full gold, the flesh is now brown,
I eat it slow, every bite I've earned down.
Your back's been screaming since the morning ache,
but you still sit there, waiting for a break.
You shift your weight on the old office chair,
and finally breathe in some fresh air.
I sent a message—no reply, just a ghost,
my last birthday invite was never a host.
They all said "always" but now they're all done,
even the dog's gone, and there's only one.
She answers the bell before the dawn breaks through,
barefoot on the cold, familiar lawn, still new.
Her voice cuts through the dark, a word said clear,
she remembers every time it rang that year.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She hums every word as the ad hits the tune,
the sky's still lit soft beneath the moon.
She taps her fingers to the steady beat,
and sings loud while the city lights meet.
He spreads the butter and makes a huge mess,
though the toaster's still warm and he says "yes."
The butter runs down the hot toast pane,
he can't tell a good slice from a plain.
You'd steal a kiss while slicing bread,
warm from the oven, slow and spread.
You'd pull me close when the silence was near,
and I knew then you were always dear.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: I hear her voice in the quiet of the call,
the years slip down like snow in a slow fall.
I hold the memory like a thread in my head,
and still remember how she'd tuck me in, instead.
She hits rewind with a little click,
her fingers move fast, the music's in quick.
The tape spins back to where she wants it to be,
she hums along, making the moment feel free.
I watched it leap—what a show, what a splash,
then disappeared in a liquid dash.
It was barely there, now it's back in the pool,
still playing king of the water, so cool.
You claim this is comfort, but it's just a zone
where you hide from the world, feeling all alone.
You sit there in silence, half asleep in your chair,
pretending the story's still worth the wasted air.
They typed "lol" after the joke was flat,
too late to matter, just a click at the chat.
Their fingers froze when the group went slack,
silence returned—no one came back.
The bagging area's a total mess,
and everyone's moving with stress.
I stand still, stuck in this slow pace,
no room to breathe or find a bit of space.
She stayed up late, her voice still so deep,
though exhaustion weighed her down to sleep.
She spoke the truth, not flinching from the view,
of all she'd carried, heavy but true.
You let it sniff the edge of your garden's wide
fence, where the air still holds the last light inside.
It licks your shoe with a soft, wet mark,
and walks back with its tail in the dark.
I sent it at midnight—no delay, no sound,
just a quiet tap that fell to the ground.
I waited for the reply, but didn't stop,
let my pride settle in, like a soft drop.
You sink into the couch with your head on the rest,
warmth flows through you like a soft, quiet chest.
You drift where your thoughts become a gentle dream,
time slips away like a river with no stream.
She stands barefoot where the rain hits hiss,
and lets the cold spark her skin with a kiss.
She watches the puddles grow long with the wait,
unsure if this moment was meant to be fate.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You keep digging through your bag for the change,
but the receipt's gone—just something strange.
You almost feel it, like a ghostly trace,
a quiet reminder of a small act of grace.
A smear runs down the kid's chipped lip,
she licks it clean but leaves another drip.
Her fingers stick to the bread like glue,
they're tangled in the jelly, all the way through.
It holds the air like it owns every still,
each drop of light sways beneath the hill.
It cuts the breeze with a motion so glide,
no space too small, no sky too wide.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You unfurl the map and the dust floats in air,
You settle into your favorite chair.
You trace a path through the worn-out trail,
And dream of the train that once ran on rail.
You think your voice sounds deep and so sore,
but it cracks when you try to walk through the door.
You try to impress, but it's clear as a show,
your vocal cords just won't grow up, though.
The system keeps misreading their face,
but they still walk in with quiet grace.
It says "access denied" — it's clearly wrong,
and still they stand, no fear, no weak song.
Her hands won't stop their quiet shake,
the silence stretches out like a lake.
We stare at the space between us, a gap,
she's tracing roads on a mental map.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You dig deep and pull out a crumpled old grin,
a faded receipt stuck to the last pin.
It's not much, but you smile at the sudden spot,
warm as a secret, still quietly hot.
You used to snore through storms and fall asleep,
a steady rhythm, soft but thick as deep.
Now quiet fills the room—no need to be bold,
just echoes of your breath, now gentle and old.
I stare at the pile that I can't quite feed,
another month, another long need.
I leave it there, let it sit on the stack,
until my hands finally pull it back.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You lean so close I feel your breath so near,
I should move but I don't want to be clear.
I let the moment stretch, then I softly sigh,
our silence floats like stars against the sky.
The screen still hums with a faint digital glow,
I let the messages whisper through the slow.
It's just a friend asking if I'm okay—
and I let my breath fall into the fray.
They stare at the screen, eyes glazed from the steam,
convinced this late-night grind is their dream.
Half the mug's gone—still sipping that slug,
like caffeine's a life sentence, not a drug.
You ordered wine but forgot the toast,
the waiter left you staring at a ghost.
You smiled and said, "That's okay—I'll still find
my way through this mess with a lightened mind."
You wipe the fog and your face appears in steam,
the haze lifts slow, and the dream starts to seem
possible—just a breath, and the glass turns clear,
hope's not far, it's just beyond the near.
My thumb finds the send button, a quiet grin,
I hope they laugh like we used to back in the kin.
The screen lights up—someone replies in chat,
I'm not alone, not lost, not stuck in that.
The pot's too close to the stove's edge,
I swore I'd keep it from the ledge.
I hover, waiting for the lip to tip,
my hands freeze—no time to flip.
You think you're so clever walking in a line,
like some tiny army with a shared design.
But your path's a mess, and now you've lost the trail,
every step you take just makes you fail.
Frost creeps up the windowpane, thick and slow,
A shadow moves where the heat used to go.
She pulls her blanket tight, though it's thin as a sheet,
Her breath turns to ice before the cold can't be beat.
